quiz.q: Why does Friedrich Merz link the EU's 2028–34 budget to Ukraine funding?
options: Germany wants to leave the EU budget
Germany wants every member state, not just a few big donors, to share the cost of Ukraine's 2027 gap, and the budget needs unanimity
EU law requires Ukraine to be funded from the budget
Germany wants to cut cohesion funds for Poland
quiz.explain: The long-term budget needs every member's consent, which gives Berlin leverage. [[p:Friedrich Merz]] wants all states to commit to Ukraine money; Slovakia and Czechia, which opted out of earlier loan guarantees, call the linkage blackmail.

quiz.q: What was new about the US question Zelenskyy says he was asked?
options: It offered Ukraine EU membership in 2027
It linked NATO membership to Ukraine giving up Donbas, a trade Russia has long ruled out
It proposed a ceasefire along the Dnipro
It asked Ukraine to hold elections first
quiz.explain: [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says it was the first time membership was tied to territory in the talks. Moscow treats Ukraine in [[p:NATO]] as a red line, so the idea faces resistance from both sides.

quiz.q: Why did Europeans care whether they sit at the main table or in a side room at the next round of Ukraine talks?
options: Side rooms have no interpreters
Any settlement on sanctions, guarantees and frozen assets would need European money and enforcement, so they want to shape it, not just be briefed
EU law bans side-room meetings
Russia demanded Europeans attend
quiz.explain: In Abu Dhabi, Europeans met US and Ukrainian officials but not Russia. In Dublin, leaders agreed a mixed team of EU officials and the E5 so that Europe negotiates directly.

quiz.q: What makes the planned Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen hard to turn into an arms-control deal?
options: China has more warheads than the US
China says it is unfair to join three-way cuts while the US and Russia hold far larger arsenals
Russia has left the UN
The meeting is only about trade
quiz.explain: China has a few hundred warheads against several thousand each for the US and Russia, and Beijing says the two biggest holders should cut first. That gap is why analysts expect little substance.

quiz.q: Why does Europe's gas-storage level matter more this winter than usual?
options: Storage was full but prices are rising
Stocks entered winter at their lowest since 2013 while the Iran war has cut LNG flows through Hormuz, leaving less buffer for a cold spell
The EU banned all gas imports
Germany switched off its storage sites
quiz.explain: The [[p:International Energy Agency]] warns that tight LNG supply and competition with Asia could push prices up during demand spikes. Germany, the biggest consumer, started winter at only 61%.
